TBG provides a suite of resources to help CMEC members and community leaders develop excellent art and music instruction for their students. With a grant from the National Endowment for the Humanities we will deepen and extend our reach by creating three new artists, composers, and song lesson guides, along with their music playlists and artist prints, hold three virtual meetings specifically for community leaders, three term instructional videos, and seasonal newsletters to reach 100 TBG community groups supporting over 1,000 children across the country and 5,000 children through our CMEC membership.

Grant.ProjectDesc: Exploring the establishment of religious freedom by the Founding Fathers through US treaties with the Barbary States. A conference on and publication of the translation of

early years of the United States, undertaken by the East-West Foundation in Slidell,
Louisiana.

Grant.ProjectTitle: Loyalists & Liberty: Savannah in the American Revolution
Grant.Program: Cooperative Agreements and Special Projects (Challenge Grants)
Grant.ProjectDesc: In anticipation of the nation’s Semiquincentennial, Coastal Heritage Society will open the exhibition “Loyalists & Liberty: Savannah in the American Revolution” in July 2026. As a centerpiece of Savannah History Museum, the 3,000-square-foot exhibition will tell the story of Savannah’s role in America’s founding and fight for independence while providing a focal point of community engagement. It will showcase rare artifacts from the 18th century that represent life during the period, including never-before-exhibited artillery that will serve as the centerpiece of the exhibition. CHS respectfully requests support for the mounting and exhibition of these artifacts critical to the story of Savannah and Georgia’s role in the War for Independence.
Grant.ToSupport:
An exhibition of 18th-century artifacts and never-before-shown
artillery to illustrate Georgia’s role in the War for Independence at the
Savannah History Museum, Georgia.

Grant.ProjectTitle: University of St. Thomas Honors Program Expansion
Grant.ProjectDesc: the University of St. Thomas is planning a strategic expansion of the Honors Program, intended to double the number of student cohorts, and providing direct student engagement in local leadership and service.

Grant.ProjectTitle: Virtuous Citizens: Building a Foundation for Virtue and Leadership at Providence College
Grant.ProjectDesc: The Humanities Program at Providence College requests a Chairman’s Award from the NEH in the 2025-26 academic year to support activities celebrating American principles and exceptionalism on the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. Activities include three related areas of program development. First, in the classroom: weekly reading seminars—one for students and one for faculty and administration—on a primary or contemporary work addressing American ideals and institutions. Second, across campus: two Humanities Forum lectures bringing in noteworthy scholars to speak on aspects of our nation’s founding, political liberty, and civic virtue. Third, around the country: a new leadership development program for sophomores in the Moab Desert in Utah integrating works and ideas from the American Founding.
Grant.ToSupport: Reading seminars, lectures, and a student leadership development program focused on American principles and exceptionalism.

An expansion and reinterpretation of the

Grant.Institution: National Museum of American Religion, Inc.

The primary presenters will be members of the Religion and America’s 250th Coalition: representatives from religious libraries, archives, and historical societies. Using primary sources from their holdings, they will share their faith’s participation in (as applicable) and theological understanding (as applicable) of the country’s founding. Additionally, several university-affiliated American religious history scholars will share general understandings of the topic according to the latest scholarship.
Grant.ToSupport: A conference to be held in spring 2026 on the roles religions played during the United States’ founding era, featuring scholars and representatives from religious libraries, archives, and historical societies.

Grant.ProjectTitle: Jews and the Persianate World: Politics, Culture, and Historical Ties

The event aims to revive suppressed narratives, spark new conversations, and promote understanding across cultures and borders. Objectives - Deepen Academic Understanding: Facilitate rigorous scholarly discourse among historians, theologians, political scientists, and cultural experts. - Foster Dialogue: Create space for thoughtful exchange between academics, policymakers, and civil society representatives. - Promote Cultural Exchange: Highlight the shared heritage and long-standing
Grant.ToSupport: A conference in September 2025 on the history of Jewish communities within the Persianate world, encompassing Iran, Afghanistan, and Central Asia.

Grant.ProjectTitle: Civics and Humanities
Grant.ProjectDesc: Acrimonious debate is tearing America apart. Respect for difference of opinion is in a tailspin, complemented by declining understanding of civics – the ideals of American government and the rights and duties of citizenship. Recent surveys reveal a commonly poor level of American civics knowledge. Universities, which should be places of healthy debate and citizenship preparation, are themselves being torn apart by political and cultural conflict. American universities have lost much of the esteem they once held as bastions of open inquiry and free exchange.  We share the view of an increasing number of people, inside and outside academia, that there is a connection between declining civics education in colleges and universities and declining public confidence in these institutions.
Grant.ToSupport: No to support statement

Grant.ProjectTitle: Bible in the American Founding

Led by our Gaylord Professor of Public Policy, Dr. Abbylin Sellers, this multi-part project is perfectly timed to help celebrate America’s 250th birthday. Each of the lectures will be public, engaging students, faculty, alumni, and the broader public to learn anew about this exceptional aspect of the American Project: the ability to combine faith and freedom.
Grant.ToSupport: A speaker series through the 2025-2026 academic year, featuring five scholars highlighting the central importance of the Christian faith and the Bible to the American Founding.

Grant.ProjectTitle: Civics and America 101 at the Heinz History Center

An expansion of the permanent American

Grant.ProjectTitle: America at 250: Service and Civics at the Intrepid Museum
Grant.Program: Cooperative Agreements and Special Projects (Challenge Grants)

Programs will include student sessions featuring veteran speakers, as well as educator- and curator-led activities for families centered around the Museum’s poignant Veterans Day, Pearl Harbor, and May, Pearl Harbor and Memorial Day ceremonies.

innovation, and perseverance at the Intrepid Museum, New York, New York.

Grant.ProjectTitle: Pathways to Independence, 1765-1777 Exhibit at HSP

The exhibit will feature original manuscripts that document the transformation of American colonists from loyal British subjects in the early 1760s to revolutionaries calling for independence by 1776. This grant request includes the costs of curating, fabricating and installing the exhibit, digitizing selected items for an online gallery, developing signature programs that will accompany the exhibit, and marketing and promoting the exhibit and programs to reach a wide audience.

An exhibition and speakers program centered on

Grant.Institution: Literary Classics of the United States
Grant.ProjectTitle: The Living Declaration: A Biography of America’s Founding Text
Grant.Program: Cooperative Agreements and Special Projects (Challenge Grants)
Grant.ProjectDesc: No text is as essential as the Declaration of Independence to understanding our history as a people and the unique contribution our political culture has made to the world. Yet the vivid historical writings that show how it came to be, and why it has remained a cultural and political touchstone, have never been available in an accessible format designed for a wide readership. Library of America requests a grant to support editorial development and publication of a book for general readers to meet this need. Informed by rigorous scholarship and designed to be one of the definitive publications of the 250th anniversary commemoration, The Living Declaration: A Biography of America’s Founding Text will trace how our national charter has defined and shaped the democratic aspirations of Americans and others for over two centuries. As the nation marks 250 years of independence, The Living Declaration will encourage us to look anew at a vital American text whose history is still unfolding.
Grant.ToSupport:
The editorial development and publication by
Library of America of a book for general readers featuring 60 excerpts of
influential figures from the 18th-20th centuries as well as short interpretive
essays that illustrate the enduring significance of the Declaration of
Independence.

With support from a Celebrate America! grant to match support already received, FAIC will develop and present twelve new training webinars and support a moderated online community forum where collections caretakers can post questions to be answered by a cadre of experts.

A year-long initiative of public programs
including exhibits, speaker events, film screenings, and air show celebrating

in Garden City, New York.

Grant.ProjectTitle: ‘One Single Place’: New Orleans, Louisiana, and the Shaping of the Early American Republic (1795-1815).
Grant.Program: Cooperative Agreements and Special Projects (Challenge Grants)
Grant.ProjectDesc: ‘One Single Place’: New Orleans, Louisiana, and the Shaping of the Early American Republic (1795-1815) is a historical exhibition that celebrates the founding of the early American Republic and the integration of New Orleans and the Mississippi River Valley into the bourgeoning country. The goal of the exhibition is to explore an overlooked aspect of the forming of the American Republic, which is the rapid integration of previous “outposts” founded by France and Spain into a central part of the American nation, and the effects those places had on transforming the perception of being American. This exhibition, featuring reproductions of navigation maps, urban plans, and architectural renderings from the Historic New Orleans Collection and Library of Congress, will be presented in New Orleans from December 2025 to March 2026 to celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.

Grant.ProjectTitle: The Hippocratic Society Curriculum Expansion & Development

Our medical curriculum is case-based focusing on various virtues that are core to being a physician. Our hope for this next year is to integrate art into our curriculum, similarly, as a “third thing” for trainees and attendings to reflect together on the what, why, and how of each virtue. Additionally, we hope to build out an additional aspect of the curriculum, on fundamental questions for practicing medicine.

A series of educational workshops and walking
tours focused on early American history for homeschool students and youth from
rural Appalachian communities by the Bloomsburg Children’s Museum, located in

Key activities include creating: * Professionally designed exhibit panels on the American Revolution’s service legacy * Plug-and-play exhibit templates for local customization * A feature video discussing service's vital role in American history * A civic engagement toolkit with guidance for public exhibits and programs * Dissemination at 2 key conferenes  The project's humanities focus is on service as a cornerstone of American democracy, demonstrating its relevance from 1776 to the present and fostering a deeper appreciation for democracy as a participatory endeavor. Grant.ProjectTitle: Princeton Battlefield Society's Experience the Battle of Princeton Reenactments

Grant.Institution: Center for the Study of Technology and Society Inc
Grant.ProjectTitle: The Lonely Neighborhood: An essay series on making the built environment more conducive to living well together
Grant.ProjectDesc: Americans are living ever more isolated lives. We get married later, start families later, have fewer children, and report more loneliness than ever before. Everyone suspects that new technology has something to do with this. But what if we’re also suffering from the failure of a very old technology?  Somehow it has become astonishingly expensive to buy a house in the United States. The median house sale price is now $417,000. Fifty years ago, in today’s dollars, it was $232,000. And the young are getting priced out: In 1981, the median first-time homebuyer was 29 years old. Today he or she is 38.  There is a dearth of original reporting on these issues, especially from publications shaped by the humanities and addressing perennial yet pressing concerns about dignity, the nature of the good life, and meaning and purpose. To help fill this gap in the ideas marketplace, The New Atlantis is publishing a series of originally reported articles called “The Lonely Neighborhood.”
Grant.ToSupport: Writing a series of journal articles on the social impact of human loneliness in housing policy and practices.

Grant.ProjectTitle: The Kingdom of Culture: Education, Slavery, and the Free Exercise of the Imagination
Grant.ProjectDesc: This project explores the historical and literary relationship between religious liberty, liberal education, and American civil rights in the long 19th century; it seeks to recover the history of a transatlantic network of black and white humanists who developed political and literary initiatives to rally opposition to slavery and propagate the ethics of a free society. Within the grant period, I intend to focus on this conversation in its colonial and antebellum context. Building on the work of Wilson Jeremiah Moses, Brycchan Carey, Peter Wirzbicki, and David Withun, among others, this project aims to desegregate our collective memory of that conversation and integrate black humanists into a transatlantic discourse about the ethics and aesthetics of education in a free society.
Grant.ToSupport: Research and writing of a book on the relationship between religious liberty, liberal education, and American civil rights in the nineteenth century.

Grant.ProjectTitle: The American Family's Almanac of Animals Book Project to Celebrate the Semiquincentennial of the United States
Grant.ProjectDesc: The American Family’s Almanac of Animals (working title) celebrates the 250th Anniversary of our country with a beautifully illustrated almanac that depicts the flora, fauna, geography, and folk-history of our country while featuring the text—and thus the self-evident principles—of our Declaration of Independence. Grant.ProjectTitle: Unsung Patriots: The Forgotten Stories of Jewish Heroes of America’s First Century
Grant.ProjectDesc: Before the Declaration of Independence was signed, before George Washington led the Continental Army, before the phrase “We the People” was ever conceived—Jews were already here. They came in search of something more radical than mere safety. They came seeking liberty. And in doing so, they helped build the very republic that promised it. Grant.ProjectTitle: Letters from Mechelen
Grant.ProjectDesc: Letters from Mechelen is a true account of a prominent Jewish family’s escape from Germany during the Holocaust. Prior to World War II, Löwensohn-Verlag, located in Fürth, Bavaria, was the largest children’s book publisher in Germany. By 1937, however, with Jews prohibited from the publishing industry, owner Gustav Löwensohn was forced to sell the company, worth three-quarters of a million Reichsmarks.  The Löwensohn family fled with almost nothing, escaping to Holland and Belgium, where they hid in attics and basements. Ultimately, the family isolated themselves in rural Belgium until 1945. After WW II, they immigrated to Kansas City, MO, and became US naturalized citizens. Unfortunately, even carrying counterfeit identification, Grandfather Gustav was suddenly arrested in Brussels in 1942, and taken to the Mechelen transit camp (Kazerne Dossin) in Belgium, where a year later, he was deported to Auschwitz concentration camp and executed.
Grant.ToSupport: Research and writing of a book about a Jewish family’s escape from Germany during the Holocaust.

Grant.ProjectTitle: Juan de Mariana, The Last Great Spanish Thinker
Grant.ProjectDesc: The Jesuit priest Juan de Mariana may have been the last of the great Spanish figures of the Spanish Golden Age. Born in Talavera de la Reina in 1535, Mariana was an illegitimate child. Early on it was clear that the young Juan was an outstanding student. At 17 he entered the University of Alcala de Henares, where, just a few years before Cardinal Francisco Jiménez de Cisneros, the founder of the University, had brought together many of the most learned Bible scholars in Europe to prepare the Biblia Políglota Complutense, the first of the great Early Modern polyglot bibles. While still very young, Mariana would begin to study the original languages of Biblical texts and many years later he would be regarded as one of the most impressive scholars in Spain. This grant will allow me to complete a biography of Mariana.
Grant.ToSupport: Research and writing for a biography of Juan de Mariana (1536-1624), Spanish priest and historian.

Grant.ProjectTitle: My Lives As a Jew: A Memoir of Identity in History
Grant.ProjectDesc: The project is a historically situated memoir about being Jewish in America and, more broadly, in modernity. I was raised in a Modern Orthodox community in suburban New Jersey and came of age in high school and college in a pluralistic Zionist youth movement. As an adult, I have lived yet another version of the modern Jewish story, that of the writer and intellectual who, while neither practicing nor affiliating, remains intensely conscious of his Jewishness. When I say that the memoir will be historically situated, I mean that it will not just be my story. I will be offering my narrative, in effect, as a synecdoche for larger ones. What is Modern Orthodoxy, that compromise formation with its oxymoronic name? What are, or were, the American Zionist youth movements, and why did they exert so strong a pull on Jewish young adults in the decades after the establishment of the State of Israel? What is the arc of the Jewish experience of modernity over the last two centuries?
Grant.ToSupport: Research for and writing of a book about being Jewish in America and, more broadly, the Jewish experience in modernity.

Grant.ProjectDesc: We intend to develop an AI research tool that will apply artificial intelligence to the study of Soviet espionage in America. It will enable researchers to integrate material from numerous publicly available sources- the Venona decryptions, Vassiliev Notebooks, Mitrokhin Archive, FBI files, Congressional Hearings, and Espionage trials- into a searchable database that will allow tracing individuals and groups, expose patterns of recruitment of spies, and information to which they had access. Not only will it provide a comprehensive overview of the targets of Soviet espionage, but it will pinpoint official misinformation and errors. This tool will serve as a prototype for applying AI to primary source documentation across the humanities.
Grant.ToSupport: Development and testing of an artificial intelligence tool to research the history of Soviet espionage in the United States.

Grant.ProjectTitle: AMCHA Initiative - AI Digital Documentation Project
Grant.ProjectDesc: This project will use artificial intelligence (AI), with human review, to preserve online campus materials and present them as trustworthy, easy-to-use records. Specifically, it will: 1) Develop a campus newspaper pipeline to improve accuracy, filtering, and classification across thousands of articles that refer to antisemitic activity;  2) Develop an Instagram pipeline to capture publicly available posts from eligible campus-affiliated accounts, in compliance with platform policies; 3) Apply advanced AI methods using large language models (LLMs), optical character recognition (OCR), and entity extraction, to transform the fragmented digital artifacts from the newspaper and Instagram content into coherent, contextualized records; 4) Archive and preserve these records in AMCHA Initiative’s public database, ensuring stable, open access; 5) Assess additional policy-compliant sources of antisemitic activity for future phases.
Grant.ToSupport: No to support statement

Grant.ProjectTitle: Villanova University Honors Program Vocare Summer Fellowship: Expansion Project
Grant.ProjectDesc: The Vocare Summer Fellowship Expansion Project will pair students with organizations that foster civic, communal, and religious engagement, and enable them to accept unpaid internships. Students will also be offered a new fall 1-credit course that will pair them with a mentor in their field, help them connect their summer experience to their wider search for meaningful work, and introduce them to local adults who will serve as concrete professional role models. Pairing these summer work experiences with a course on vocation will widen their professional imaginations, encourage them to seek work that fosters the common good, and deepen their professional discernment.

Grant.ProjectTitle: Two Nations Under God: How [Biblical] Israel Inspires the United States
Grant.ProjectDesc: This book will feature essays on how presidents have framed the holiday of Hanukkah as a beacon of light for all US citizens, the scriptural influence of the American eagle, the Hebrew Bible and presidential inaugural addresses, the Exodus story of America’s unifying national narrative, Queen Esther’s enduring influence on both sides of the political aisle, Abraham Lincoln’s biblical rhetoric, the White House and the wisdom of Genesis, and many related topics.
Grant.ToSupport: Research and writing toward a book for nonacademic audiences on the relationship between Hebraic ideas and the American experiment.

Grant.ProjectTitle: Unsung Patriots: Stories of the Jewish Patriots of the American Revolution
Grant.ProjectDesc: The Unsung Patriots podcast series will offer the hidden history of the beginnings of Jewish American life in the Revolutionary era. Each episode will narrate the life and legacy of one of the eight Jewish patriots and the two major Jewish locations of that era: the Mikveh Israel synagogue in Philadelphia and the Touro Synagogue in Newport. They will consist of short essays accompanied by interviews, music, and read-outs of historical transcripts. The podcasts will be released on a weekly basis beginning in June 2026 to honor the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States of America.

Grant.ProjectTitle: Iran's Virtual Museum of Modernity
Grant.ProjectDesc: This project involves the development of a 3-year strategic plan for a digital humanities archive, which will explore the Persian Enlightenment Era from the mid-19th century to the early 20th century. The project, entitled Iran’s Virtual Museum of Modernity, will highlight an often-overlooked aspect of the ancient nation’s history: its rich engagement with modernity, civil society, and secularism. The museum will focus on three central historical pillars during Persia’s hidden era: first, its unique relationship with the United States, and the cross-cultural exchanges that led to the development of civil society in Persia; second, the proliferation of new cultural movements, reflected in the literary works of writers and philosophers who explored modern themes; and finally, economic modernization—namely, the transition away from a semi-feudal arrangement toward industrialization and capitalism.
